note: The seat holds the body upright, so supportive is more exact than comfortable or spacious. Feedback connects the three words to posture, general feeling and room. Suitable Bronze precision decision.

The slow change supports gradual. Smooth is plausible because the stem vaguely asks about “the change itself”, but no lack of jumps is stated. Ask which word specifically describes how slowly the lights dim. The feedback draws the right pace/continuity distinction.

A practical fix that helps gives evidence of constructive feedback. Encouraging could describe tone and detailed could describe amount, neither established. Distractor feedback teaches these differences.
Crisp captures a light crunch without difficulty biting. Firm could describe pressure and tough conflicts with ease of biting. Good concise context and feedback at Bronze.

Deeply moving is the familiar idiom. “Highly moving” is possible but less natural here, as the feedback says, and “strongly moving” is awkward. Show the sentence as its own vocabulary gap and ask which phrase sounds most natural.

A room fills up; a crowd builds up; people pack out a room. Feedback is specific and correct. A and B largely test subject/verb combinations rather than process. Present the sentence in its own gap and clarify that the room is the subject.

The key is the only idiomatic choice. Both distractors are artificial. Use equally natural expressions for different effects, such as holding attention, building tension and moving the audience, then ask which expresses sustained interest. Keep the precise meaning distinction in feedback.

Good value is the only idiomatic phrase. Valuable price and worthy cost are transparent throwaways. Compare natural expressions such as “low-priced”, “worth the price” and “free to join” using a clear price and set of benefits.

The quieter lines and the back of the room remain. B overgeneralises; C attributes a cause to performance. “Keeps the extent” is opaque. Show the original and three revisions, and ask which keeps the same listening difficulty without blaming the actors.

Only B preserves two and the visit. A makes a broader claim; C invents a history. Ask which version still says how many exhibits were affected and when. Revision comparison can make the contrast easier to scan without highlighting the key.

A preserves occasional first-person difficulty. B universalises across the explanations and C generalises to other readers. The feedback identifies the relevant change. Useful practice distinguishing strength, frequency and viewpoint.
Only C preserves the one-hour maximum. A permits longer and B turns it into an exact duration. The feedback cleanly distinguishes these meanings and the practical example supports transfer.

B addresses students directly and retains the reader-specific condition. A is cautious but formal; C assumes enjoyment. Ask which ending speaks directly to students and still says who would enjoy the film. Preserve the feedback’s account of both dimensions.

B is the friendliest advice, but C also criticises crowding without attacking staff. The question asks about blame while the key partly depends on register. Supply the crowded seating observation and ask which is both friendly and useful to readers. Use plausible alternatives that differ by audience or practical advice.

C naturally recommends the course to people who can make time to practise. A uses viewing for a course and B is excessively formal, so they offer little Silver challenge. Add a specific demanding feature and compare fair advice for different students.

Only A reports the fifteen-minute wait exactly and gives usable advice. B exaggerates, C makes a broad formal judgement, and both are conspicuous. Use narrower overstatements or time shifts as distractors so the item teaches proportional criticism.

C changes severity without changing time and place. A paraphrases and B extends the time. Feedback supports the key, but this single decision repeats Silver intensity and scope work. Ask learners to select a revision for a new audience, then explain which detail and degree of criticism they retained.
